summary:
Roflare is a web-based application that visualizes and analyzes satellite thermal anomaly detections from NASA FIRMS, using MODIS and VIIRS Suomi-NPP data.

The platform combines detections from both satellite sources and identifies potential associations based on geographic proximity and observation time. Using a graph-based matching approach, it groups related detections into connected components, helping users explore how different satellite observations may correspond to the same thermal event.

An interactive map displays individual detections, spatial relationships, and matched groups, while analytical visualizations provide additional insight into the collected data.

By bringing multiple satellite data sources together in one interface, Roflare makes thermal anomaly data easier to explore, compare, and interpret. It aims to support faster analysis and improve situational awareness, while recognizing that satellite thermal anomalies do not necessarily represent confirmed fires.
details:
Project Details – Roflare

Roflare is an interactive web platform designed to make satellite-based thermal anomaly data easier to explore and analyze. It uses data from NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), combining observations from two satellite instruments: MODIS and VIIRS aboard the Suomi-NPP satellite.

How it works

The backend processes satellite detection records collected from NASA FIRMS and compares observations from the two sources. It identifies candidate associations using two criteria: geographic distance (up to 1 km) and observation time difference (up to 60 minutes).

Rather than treating each detection independently, Roflare models the associations as a graph, where detections represent nodes and potential cross-satellite matches represent edges. Connected components are then identified and presented as groups of related observations. This approach supports one-to-many and many-to-many relationships, allowing multiple detections from different satellite sources to be explored together.

The frontend provides an interactive map displaying individual detections, candidate associations, and grouped observations. Users can explore geographic relationships, inspect detection details, and access analytical visualizations that help reveal patterns in the collected data.

Benefits and intended impact

Satellite instruments can observe the same thermal event at different times and locations. Analyzing their observations together provides a broader perspective than examining each dataset separately.

Roflare aims to:

  • Bring observations from multiple satellite sources into a unified interface.
  • Reveal potential relationships between detections that might otherwise be examined independently.
  • Make large volumes of satellite data easier to explore and interpret.
  • Support situational awareness and provide an accessible starting point for further investigation.

An important consideration is that thermal anomalies are not necessarily confirmed fires. Roflare identifies potential associations between satellite observations; it does not independently confirm fire events or predict their spread.

Technologies and tools

The project was developed using:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS.
  • Mapping: Leaflet and React Leaflet.
  • Data visualization: Recharts.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Data processing: Pandas and graph-based matching algorithms.
  • Data source: NASA FIRMS, using MODIS Standard Processing (MODIS_SP) and VIIRS Suomi-NPP Standard Processing (VIIRS_SNPP_SP).
  • Data storage: CSV datasets.

Creativity and design considerations

The main technical idea behind Roflare is the cross-satellite association approach. Instead of simply displaying detections as separate points on a map, the application analyzes their spatial and temporal relationships to build groups of potentially related observations.

During development, we considered geographic accuracy, observation time differences, the possibility of multiple detections corresponding to the same event, data volume, and map performance. We also focused on making the interface intuitive, allowing users to move from a broad overview to individual detection details without overwhelming them with raw satellite records.

Roflare combines satellite data processing, graph-based analysis, and interactive geospatial visualization into a single platform, making NASA FIRMS data more accessible and useful for exploration.
